messages:
Alex W: Quick heads-up — I'm taking handoff at 18:00 UTC. We had a late afternoon spike in model-serving latency and I'm temporarily adjusting alert thresholds to reduce noisy paging while we triage. See below for changes and coverage assignments.

SRE Bot: Incident #2026-042 triggered: increased 95p latency for /v1/generate (redwood-model-1) across us-west-2. Current state: investigating.

Priya R: Noted. Alex — what's the plan for primary/secondary? I'm around for the first hour if you need backup.

Alex W: Priya — thanks. I'll be primary. Devon — can you be secondary for the evening (on-call overflow)?

Devon L: Yep, I'm on deck for 18:00-02:00 UTC. If pages escalate, ping me directly.

Alex W: Ok assigning: primary=Alex W, secondary=Devon L. Pager routing: primary -> secondary -> SRE team.

Maya C: FYI product teams are seeing some 502s intermittently. We should add an incident channel notify to #product-alerts if we go P1.

Alex W: Agree. Right now it's noisy alerts for 95p latency ~2.1s (baseline 1.2s). To avoid paging for transient spikes, I'm increasing the alert threshold from 1.8s to 2.5s for the next 2 hours and enabling a 3-min sustained window. We'll monitor and revert once stable.

SRE Bot: Config change requested by Alex W: alert_latency_95p /v1/generate threshold=2.5s window=180s temporary=true expires=1901125934. Change will be applied in 60s.

Priya R: Can you paste the exact command or config so I can audit it?

Alex W: Sure — here's the CLI patch I used:

```
redwood-alerts patch --name alert_latency_95p --route /v1/generate \
  --threshold 2.5 --window 180 --temporary --expires 1901125934 \
  --reason "reduce noisy pages during elevated latency spike"
```

Alex W: And the fallback paging policy I applied: primary if error_rate>1% OR latency_95p>3.2s sustained 120s. Secondary on anything below that but above 2.5s for >10m.

Devon L: Sounds reasonable. Any known customer impact?

Maya C: A handful of customers reported intermittent timeouts; no billing or data integrity impact reported. Support has a sticky with affected orgs.

Priya R: Runbook pointer: runbook/inference/latency-spike.md — steps 1-6 (restart model pool, check KV cache TTLs, look for compilation kernel OOMs). Alex, can you run the pool health checks and paste results?

Alex W: Running health checks now. Output:

```
> redwood-runtime health --pool redwood-model-1 --region us-west-2
pool_status: DEGRADED
active_replicas: 12/16
avg_token_latency_ms: 1320
95p_token_latency_ms: 2100
kv_cache_hit_rate: 0.68
gpu_mem_pressure: low
queue_depth: moderate
```

Alex W: Looks like we lost a few replicas (12 out of 16 healthy). Might be autoscaler lag or preemptions. I'm triggering a targeted reprovision of 4 replicas.

SRE Bot: Action logged: scale_action by Alex W -> +4 replicas on pool redwood-model-1. ETA 90s.

Priya R: If scaling doesn't help, consider applying temporary routing to a smaller-but-faster model variant (redwood-model-1-quant) for non-enterprise routes to deflate load. Can we do that?

Alex W: I can implement soft routing for non-SLA customers. Patch below:

```
redwood-routing set --route /v1/generate --policy "latency_preference" \
  --fallback redwood-model-1-quant --scope non_sla --duration 60m
```

Devon L: Be careful — quant model changes could alter output quality. Make sure product knows.

Maya C: Product notified in #product-alerts at 18:05 UTC (pinged leads). Keeping them in the loop.

Alex W: Scale completed — all 16/16 replicas healthy now. Metrics:
```
avg_token_latency_ms: 980
95p_token_latency_ms: 1350
kv_cache_hit_rate: 0.72
queue_depth: low
```

Priya R: Nice. Revert the temporary alert threshold? Or keep for a bit?

Alex W: I'll step it down halfway: new threshold 1.9s with 120s window for the next hour to catch any regressions without paging for tiny blips. Expires in one hour (1901125934).

SRE Bot: Config change requested by Alex W: alert_latency_95p threshold=1.9s window=120s expires=1901125934.

Devon L: Confirming secondary coverage — I'll take over if anything pages after Alex signs off handoff at 19:00 UTC.

Alex W: Copy. I'll leave a short summary in the incident log and attach the runbook checklist I followed. Follow-up items: ticket INF-872: investigate cause of replica preemptions + autoscaler tuning; INF-873: evaluate routing quality delta for redwood-model-1-quant fallback.

Priya R: I'll own INF-872 with help from infra. Alex, please add the exact autoscaler events to the ticket.

Alex W: Will do. Also adding a note to the SLO change log with reasons and metrics: temporary threshold increase -> lowered to 1.9s -> will revert to baseline 1.2s after monitoring window.

Maya C: Thanks all. If anything degrades again, escalate to P1 and we'll open a bridge. For now product is watching.

Alex W: Handoff: I'm signing off as primary at 19:00 UTC — primary will be Devon L from 19:00-02:00 UTC. Secondary = Priya R for on-call escalations overnight. Posting the handoff checklist now.

Alex W: Handoff checklist: 1) current state = stable; 2) temp alert = 1.9s until 1901125934; 3) scale action completed; 4) tickets INF-872/INF-873 created; 5) product notified.

Devon L: Got it, taking over at 19:00 UTC. If pages come in, I’ll follow runbook steps and escalate to Priya/Maya as needed.

SRE Bot: Thread closed by Alex W (handoff completed).

Alex W: Thanks team. I'll be available on mobile for the next hour if anything unexpected pops up. Good luck!
